name: Dal Makhani

ingredients.name: Whole black gram (sabut urad / kali dal)
Salt
ingredients.householdMeasure: ⅓ tsp (to taste; less if your butter is salted)

ingredients.name: Fresh cream (malai / Amul fresh cream, ~25% fat)

equipment: Heavy-bottomed pan or kadai (or cook the masala in the cooker's base)
Bowl for soaking, and a sieve/colander to drain
Mixer-grinder small jar to purée the tomato
Grater for ginger and garlic (or a mortar and pestle, or a fine knife mince)
Wooden spoon or ladle (for stirring and mashing)
Measuring spoons (ordinary teaspoons and a steel tumbler are fine)
Optional for smoke: tongs, a gas flame to heat the coal, and a small steel bowl or onion skin to hold it

steps.title: Rinse the dal
steps.text: Put 40 g whole urad and 10 g rajma in a bowl and rinse 3 times, rubbing between your fingers.
steps.visualCue: the water goes from cloudy grey to only slightly grey by the third rinse
steps.cameraCheck: the rinsed lentils and beans in the bowl
steps.videoShot: hand swirling black lentils in water
steps.watchOut: skipping the rinse leaves grit and a dusty taste; if the water is still dark after 3 rinses, rinse once more.

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Cover with 300 ml water and leave at room temperature for 8–10 hours.
steps.tip: rajma must be well soaked. Undercooked rajma is hard to digest and can cause stomach upset.
steps.visualCue: urad and rajma about doubled in size; rajma skin smooth and plump
steps.watchOut: a soak much longer than 12 h in a hot kitchen can turn the water sour or frothy (a sour smell); in summer soak in the fridge, or drain and rinse if it smells off.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Pour off the soaking water through a sieve and rinse once.
steps.visualCue: drained, glossy lentils with clear run-off water
steps.videoShot: water poured off through a sieve
steps.watchOut: cooking in the soaking water, which is bitter and can upset digestion; always discard it.

steps.title: Load the cooker
steps.text: Put the drained dal in the pressure cooker with 300 ml fresh water and half the salt (1 g).
steps.visualCue: water about 3 cm above the lentils; cooker no more than half full
steps.videoShot: water poured over the dal in the cooker
steps.watchOut: filling the cooker past half, since frothing dal can clog the vent; if foam rises near the lid, add ½ tsp oil or butter to calm it and reduce the flame.

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Close the lid and cook on high until the first whistle, then turn to low and cook 25–30 min.
steps.visualCue: a steady whistle, then only a gentle hiss on low
steps.watchOut: a constant loud whistling or spluttering means the flame is too high; turn it down at once or the dal can scorch at the bottom.

steps.title: Let the pressure drop
steps.text: Turn off the heat and let the pressure release on its own.
steps.visualCue: the valve settles and the hiss stops; the lid opens without force
steps.watchOut: forcing the lid or releasing steam by hand, which makes the dal spurt and the beans split unevenly; wait until the valve drops by itself.

steps.title: Check doneness
steps.text: Open the cooker, take one urad and one rajma and press each between your thumb and finger.
steps.visualCue: both mash completely with no hard centre; some urad skins have split
steps.cameraCheck: a squashed urad and rajma between your fingers
steps.watchOut: a chalky or gritty centre in the rajma, which means undercooked; add 50 ml water and cook another 10 min on low, and do not move on until it is soft.

steps.title: Mash lightly
steps.text: Mash about a third of the dal against the side with the back of the ladle.
steps.visualCue: thickened, partly creamy dal with most lentils still whole
steps.videoShot: ladle pressing lentils against the cooker wall
steps.watchOut: mashing it all into a paste, which loses the texture; stop when about two-thirds of the lentils are still whole.

steps.title: Purée the tomato
steps.text: Blend 80 g tomato to a smooth purée.
steps.visualCue: smooth, bright-red purée with no large pieces
steps.watchOut: tomato skin flecks, which stay in the masala; strain, or grate the tomato and discard the skin instead.

steps.title: Chop onion
steps.text: Finely chop 40 g onion.
steps.visualCue: small, even pieces about the size of a grain of rice
steps.watchOut: uneven chunks, which burn at the edges while the big pieces stay raw; keep pieces similar in size.

steps.title: Grate ginger and garlic, slit chilli
steps.text: Grate 5 g ginger and 2 garlic cloves; slit 1 green chilli lengthwise.
steps.visualCue: two small heaps of paste and a slit chilli still joined at the stem
steps.cameraCheck: ginger, garlic and chilli on the board
steps.watchOut: cutting the chilli right through, which scatters seeds and heat; slit only, and keep the stem on.

steps.title: Melt butter
steps.text: Heat the heavy pan on medium and add 10 g butter (2 tsp).
steps.visualCue: butter melted and foaming, a creamy nutty smell, still pale yellow
steps.watchOut: brown specks and a sharp burnt smell, which mean the pan is too hot; lift it off the heat for 10 sec, or start again if it is dark.

steps.title: Add cumin and onion
steps.text: Add ½ tsp cumin; when it sizzles (about 10 sec), add the onion and stir.
steps.visualCue: cumin sizzles and smells toasty; onion turns soft and light golden
steps.videoShot: cumin sizzling, then onion going in
steps.watchOut: dark brown cumin or onion, which turns the dal bitter; if it darkens fast, add 1 tbsp water and lower the flame.

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Stir in the grated ginger, garlic and slit chilli.
steps.visualCue: the raw garlic smell is gone and it smells fragrant
steps.watchOut: browning the garlic, which tastes bitter; keep stirring and move to the next step as soon as the raw smell is gone.

steps.title: Cook the tomato masala
steps.text: Add the tomato purée and ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder. Cook on medium, stirring often.
steps.tip: if it sticks, add 1 tbsp water, not more butter.
steps.visualCue: thick, deep-red masala that leaves the sides, with butter glistening at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: the pan, tilted to show the fat at the edge
steps.watchOut: a sour, raw tomato smell or a thin masala, which means it is undercooked; keep cooking until the butter separates at the edge.

steps.title: Combine dal and masala
steps.text: Tip the cooked dal (with its liquid) into the masala and stir. Add the remaining salt (1 g).
steps.visualCue: brown-black dal streaked with red masala, then evenly mixed
steps.watchOut: adding the dal to a very hot masala, which spits; lower the flame first and stir right away.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add up to 100 ml water so the dal is loose and pourable.
steps.visualCue: the dal runs off the ladle like thin custard
steps.cameraCheck: the ladle lifted out of the dal
steps.watchOut: adding it all at once; add in two halves, since the dal thickens a lot during the simmer and a too-thin dal can be reduced later, but a too-thick one can only be rescued with hot water.

steps.title: Slow simmer
steps.text: Simmer on the lowest flame, partly covered, stirring and scraping the bottom every 3–4 min.
steps.tip: this simmer is what makes it "makhani". Longer gives a silkier dal; more butter is not a substitute.
steps.visualCue: dal turns darker, glossy and creamy; some lentils break down and lazy bubbles plop on the surface
steps.cameraCheck: the pan at the end of the simmer
steps.videoShot: lazy bubbles in thick, dark dal
steps.watchOut: a burnt smell and dark crust at the bottom, which means it is catching; scrape, add 50 ml hot water, and do not scrape the burnt layer into the dal.

steps.title: Add cream
steps.text: Stir in 15 ml (3 tsp) fresh cream.
steps.visualCue: dal turns a lighter, velvety brown
steps.videoShot: white cream swirled in and disappearing
steps.watchOut: cream going in while the dal is boiling hard, which can leave oily streaks; lower the flame first, then stir.

steps.title: Add garam masala and kasuri methi
steps.text: Sprinkle ¼ tsp garam masala, crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan, and stir.
steps.visualCue: a warm, toasty, "restaurant-like" aroma rises
steps.watchOut: too much kasuri methi, which makes the dal bitter; keep to ½ tsp and crush rather than adding whole leaves.

steps.title: Final simmer
steps.text: Simmer 5 more min on low.
steps.visualCue: thick but still pourable; it coats the back of a spoon
steps.cameraCheck: the back of a spoon dipped in the dal
steps.videoShot: spoon lifted with a creamy coating
steps.watchOut: it tightens quickly, and a spoon that leaves a clean trail means it is too thick; stir in 2 tbsp hot water.

steps.title: (Optional) Smoke the dal
steps.text: Turn off the heat. Heat a small piece of charcoal on the gas flame with tongs until it glows red, put it in a small steel bowl set on top of the dal, pour ¼ tsp ghee on it, and close the lid at once.
steps.tip: remove the bowl and coal before serving.
steps.visualCue: thick white smoke when the ghee hits the coal
steps.cameraCheck: the small bowl sitting on the dal
steps.videoShot: ghee poured on glowing coal, lid closing
steps.watchOut: smoking beyond 3–4 min, which tastes bitter and acrid; remove the bowl and coal as soon as time is up, and open a window.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Taste for salt, pour into a bowl, top with the last 5 g butter and swirl 1 tsp (5 ml) cream on top.
steps.visualCue: dark, glossy dal with a melting butter pat and a white cream swirl
steps.videoShot: slow pan across the bowl as the butter melts
steps.watchOut: a flat taste, usually missing salt; add a pinch, stir and taste again.

reasons: Whole urad and rajma give about 15 g plant protein and about 12 g fibre per bowl, with no frying and no added sugar. The weak points are saturated fat from butter and cream (~11 g of the ~19 g fat) and sodium (~900 mg), even at FitPlate's measured 1 tbsp butter + 4 tsp cream. Restaurant versions often use several tablespoons of butter and cream per portion plus more salt, which roughly doubles the fat.

researchRating.basis: one of India's most-loved restaurant dals and a fixture on North Indian and dhaba menus; recipe pages rate very high (Cup of Yum 4.9 from 1,008 reviews, Tarla Dalal 4 from 47 reviews), with one low outlier (Zayka Ka Tadka 2.5 from 28 ratings). Common complaints: the long time and planning, dal that is "not creamy" because the urad was undercooked, and the heaviness of restaurant versions.

storage: Fridge-safe in an airtight container for 3 days (est.); it thickens and tastes better on day 2. Freezer: up to 1 month (est.), ideally before adding the final cream and butter. Reheating: on the stove on low with 3–4 tbsp water, stirring and scraping, until it bubbles gently, or 2 min in the microwave, covered, stirring halfway. Add a fresh teaspoon of cream after reheating if it looks split.
leftoverRemix: Dal makhani paratha with a cheese pull. Cook the leftover dal down until thick and almost dry, mash it, mix in chopped onion, coriander and a pinch of chaat masala, and use it as a stuffing for parathas with a little grated cheese. Cook on a tawa with ½ tsp oil per side. Alternatively, loosen it with water and use it as a "black dal soup" topped with roasted cumin and lemon.
burnOff: about 5.4 km of running (at ~70 kcal/km), or about 7.6 km of brisk walking (at ~50 kcal/km, est.). With 2 phulkas (about 550 kcal total (est.)): about 7.9 km running or 11 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: whole urad and rajma are pulses, and the recipe uses onion, garlic and table salt (common vrat rule set assumed)

ekadashi.reason: pulses and beans such as urad and rajma are avoided on Ekadashi in the common rule set (families differ)

jain.reason: drop onion, garlic and fresh ginger (root items) and use sonth; see Jain variant

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; filling and protein-rich (about 15 g), but salty (about 900 mg sodium) and rich, so keep portions modest at sehri

jain.reason: drop onion (40 g), garlic (6 g) and fresh ginger (5 g), which are root items; use sonth (dry ginger powder) instead (see Jain variant)

vegan.reason: swap butter (15 g) for oil and cream (20 ml) for cashew cream (see Vegan variant)

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian recipe, no meat or egg

sattvik.reason: skip onion, garlic and the chilli-ginger base as in the Jain variant

glutenFree.reason: urad, rajma, tomato, butter, cream and spices only; no hing is used (most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour, so do not add it)

dairyFree.reason: butter and cream are the dairy; use the Vegan variant swaps

variants.reason: Main recipe already gluten-free (no hing, no flour; if you add hing, buy a gluten-free brand).
